parsed.explanation: The combined national/division regime is high-risk but short of the 0.15 tier. The visitor faces border refusal or possible lifetime fraud ineligibility when documents or appearance raise sex doubt, and facility rules (national executive order, state bans, municipal ordinance) can lead to ejection or trespass arrest; the documented arrest ended in a men's jail and male-guard search. Custody and immigration detention show conversion-like practices, hormone removal and abuse. The division lacks gender-identity nondiscrimination and hate-crime coverage, bans minors' care, and after a 2026 mob attack charged the victims while arresting no attackers. National hate-crime law, employment protection, court injunctions and some local protections exist, but no working visitor remedy is documented before custody. The undercount-floor violence figure is not used. This sits near the 0.25 anchors, slightly below due to compounding border and local exposures.

entry_documents.exposure: National sex-binary order; foreign ministry stopped X markers; border cable requires refusal or additional evidence on sex discrepancy and flags possible permanent fraud ineligibility; reports of passports blocked and travellers stranded; trans-athlete entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires all four elements and is not automatic; litigation pending; some court injunctions.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor uses a home passport, but an X marker or appearance mismatch can trigger secondary screening, refusal, or a fraud case-note tag; national issuance rules do not bind the visitor, yet border practice does.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse; national corrections use conversion-like practices and remove hormones; division held a trans woman in a men's jail and had her searched by a male guard despite a female licence marker.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute exists; some executive orders are enjoined; no documented operative custody protection for trans visitors; the prison LGBTQ order was rescinded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate to investigation or fraud and detention; a facility arrest leads to birth-sex custody; immigration status can move a person into abusive custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars trans use of government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; multiple state bans exist, four criminal in some circumstances; the division municipality enacted a severe restroom ordinance; documented trespass arrest and men's-ward detention.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some states and localities have no bans or have protections; national hate-crime law does not address facilities; no working visitor remedy is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The harshest operative rule governs: a federal facility, state ban, or municipal ordinance can require ejection or arrest; custody then places by birth sex.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors; national executive order frames minors' care as mutilation; proposed insurance bar; prison hormone removal; hospital denied care to a trans attack victim and placed her in a men's ward; division insurance excludes transition care.
care_services.protection: Courts blocked some national orders; national employment and hate-crime law do not secure care access; no documented visitor-facing care protection in the division.
care_services.interaction: An adult needing HRT or emergency care faces records mismatch, refusal, or ward misplacement; a minor cannot lawfully receive care, forcing parents to choose between care and travel.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy lists 'radically pro-transgender' groups among priority targets; justice-department reward guidance invokes 'radical gender ideology'; executive order directs school investigations and prosecutions; division sheriff charged victims and arrested no attackers; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; national employment ruling; 22 states plus capital outlaw discrimination; some court injunctions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing and local inaction raise risk when violence occurs; national recourse may exist in theory but is not shown operating for visitors in the division.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division minors' care ban since 2024; national executive order targets teachers who facilitate social transition and school 'gender ideology'; sports ban; proposed insurance bar; public opinion supports assigned-sex documents and sports bans.
minors_guardians.protection: Some national orders are enjoined; the division has no nondiscrimination or care-access protection; national hate-crime and employment law do not secure care or school access.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a parent may face care denial, school or activity exclusion, and forced disclosure; parent or guardian inquiry is possible though direct parent prosecution is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: August 2026 mob beat a trans couple over park restroom use; victims were charged with disturbing the peace, no attacker was arrested; one was denied hospital care, held in a men's jail and searched by a male guard; local severe ordinance; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; two municipalities protect; no documented working local protection. The violence rate is only an undercount floor, so it is not used as magnitude.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response can criminalize the victim; the local ordinance legitimizes confrontation; reporting may lead to custody or outing rather than protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and border policy, facility bans, custody practices and the care ban remain operative; fraud finding is permanent with limited waiver; local charges unresolved; no state nondiscrimination law.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit, legal-aid FAQ, court injunctions, national hate-crime and employment law, existing X passports valid until expiry, some state and local protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are national and slow, not pre-custody; a visitor cannot reliably avoid summary refusal, facility arrest, or birth-sex custody; local outcomes are unpredictable.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A has an explicit deceptive-presentation crime, routine transit arrests, months of pretrial custody, beatings and a capital provision. This jurisdiction lacks a general presentation crime and a documented capital path, so it is safer, but shares abusive custody and hostile institutions; hence above 0.15.

0.25-C has birth-sex prison housing, frequent assaults, a cross-dressing arrest statute, slow remedies and no execution. This jurisdiction is similar, with birth-sex custody and facility exclusion, but adds national border-fraud risk and a recent mob attack where victims were charged; it sits slightly below 0.25.

0.55-B involves border secondary screening, refused admission, administrative penalties and an appeal desk, without documented custody abuse. This jurisdiction is lower because border doubt can produce permanent fraud ineligibility, facility arrests lead to birth-sex custody, and care denial and local violence are documented.

0.75-C offers trained border officers, brief detention, written reasons, counsel, appeals and compensation. This jurisdiction has active document refusal, facility bans, abusive custody and no working visitor remedy, so it is far below the 0.75 tier.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system compounds: a foreign passport mismatch can trigger border refusal or a fraud case note; a facility arrest in the division can produce birth-sex custody and search; emergency care can be denied or mis-warded; and local police may charge the trans victim. National hate-crime and employment protections and court injunctions are real but operate after the fact and are not shown to protect visitors in this division. Minors face additional care bans and school/transition hostility. No execution pathway is documented, so the score is above the 0.15 tier, but multiple universal-exposure and state-response harms keep it in the high-risk band.
